title: Cycles on a P–V Diagram
short: Around a closed cycle ΔU = 0, and the area enclosed is the net work.
trouble: Students add up the work of each leg without signs, so the net work comes out as the whole area under the paths.

blocks.html: An engine cannot expand forever; it must come back to where it started and go again. A path on the P–V diagram that returns to its starting state is a cycle. Using the processes you know, we can do the bookkeeping for a whole cycle.

Internal energy belongs to the state. Back at the starting $P$ and $V$, the gas is back at its starting $T$ and $U$, so $\Delta U = 0$ around any cycle. Then the first law gives $Q_{\text{net}} = -W_{\text{net}}$: the net heat that flows in equals the net work the gas does. The gas does positive work while it expands and negative work while it is compressed; if it expands at a higher pressure than it is compressed at, the difference is the area inside the loop.

Around a cycle, $\Delta U = 0$ and $Q_{\text{net}} = W_{\text{by}}$. The net work done by the gas equals the area enclosed: positive for a clockwise cycle (an engine), negative for a counterclockwise one (a refrigerator).

blocks.name: ph-pv

opts.task: Drag a corner. The enclosed area, and the net work, change together.

blocks.cap: A rectangular cycle. The table lists $Q$, $W$ and $\Delta U$ for each leg; the $\Delta U$ column adds to zero.

blocks.title: Net work of a rectangle
blocks.q: A gas goes around A $(200\,\text{kPa}, 2.0\,\text{L})$ → B $(200\,\text{kPa}, 5.0\,\text{L})$ → C $(80\,\text{kPa}, 5.0\,\text{L})$ → D $(80\,\text{kPa}, 2.0\,\text{L})$ → A. Find the net work done by the gas.
steps: B→C and D→A: constant volume, no work.

blocks.title: Bookkeeping the legs
blocks.q: For a monatomic gas on the same cycle, find $Q$ for each leg and check the totals.
steps: Use $\Delta U = \tfrac{3}{2}\Delta(PV)$ and $Q = \Delta U - W$, with $W$ on the gas.
Totals: $\Delta U = 0$, $W = -360\,\text{J}$, $Q = 1500 - 900 - 600 + 360 = 360\,\text{J}$. The net heat equals the net work by the gas.

blocks.title: A triangle
blocks.q: A gas goes from $(100\,\text{kPa}, 1.0\,\text{L})$ up to $(300\,\text{kPa}, 1.0\,\text{L})$, along a straight line to $(100\,\text{kPa}, 4.0\,\text{L})$, and back at constant pressure. Find the net work by the gas.
steps: The cycle runs clockwise, so the net work by the gas is the enclosed area, positive.

blocks.html: Adding up the work of each leg without signs, which gives the whole area under the paths ($600 + 240 = 840\,\text{J}$ above) instead of the area enclosed ($360\,\text{J}$). Expansion and compression have opposite signs. Check: the net work can never be more than the area inside the loop.
